item.nusmp.cloak_mimic_tame.card:
A living cloak (no attunement). Shapechanger (use): the cloak shifts through six cuts and colours. Protective: +2 armor and half acid damage; Tensura's Corrosion Resistance is lent to you and Corrosion cannot take hold. Alert: night vision, Tensura's Danger Sense is lent to you, and every 2 seconds up to three hostile creatures that have chosen you and are creeping up from behind glow for 2 seconds. Clingy: +0.2 knockback resistance, it holds you in place. Hungry: at the turn of each day the cloak feeds on you: a tenth of your magicules if you have them (it prefers a caster), otherwise it weighs you down for a minute (weakness, slowness). It never touches your food bar.
Became: the DC 18 Strength check to remove it is not modelled (you may take it off whenever you like); sacrificing hit dice and levels of exhaustion are magicules and the exhaustion effects; advantage on Perception is the night vision, Danger Sense and the warning glow.
item.nusmp.suit_of_the_astral_overseer.c:
Requires attunement. Light armour (6 points). You never take fall damage; Tensura's gravity and spatial attack resistances are kept while worn.
Zero Gravity Movement (switch on or off): you fly at twice the walking-flight speed. Flight costs magicules (about a tenth of a percent of your pool a second; never hunger) and ends when they run dry or you take the suit off; it never touches flight someone else gave you, and a soft landing is thrown in.
Into the Void: twice a day a spell that would hit you (magic damage) finds nothing to strike and is cancelled; you are charged with the void: Strength and Speed for 8 s and Tensura's Thought Acceleration (the old 'advantage on your next spell attack').
Traveler of the Universe: when you cross to another dimension, Nausea, Blindness, Darkness and Tensura's confusion and insanity are lifted from you and allies within 8 blocks, you get Regeneration and Resistance for a few seconds and Tensura's spatial and abnormal-condition resistances for 30 s.
Replaced: 'by a spellcaster' is not enforced; the opposing spell attack roll is the two daily wards; AC 12+modifier is the armour value.
item.nusmp.bag_of_colding.card: Wondrous item, rare. A Bag of Holding of 54 slots, but it is a cold larder: it takes only food. Carrying it cuts freezing damage by 30%. Cold Snack (with the Use Worn Relic key): eats one food item from the larder as you walk, fresh and chilled: it feeds half again as much and none of its bad side effects apply. Stuff the Bag (sneak and use, 3% mana, 30 s cooldown): the nearest small foe in front of you is pinned inside for three seconds. At each of three pulses (the 'end of each minute') it rolls a save against the bag (55% to fail, less with knockback resistance); a failed one deals 4 cold damage and frostbite and chills it (Tensura). A foe that fails twice of three gains the card's level of exhaustion: Mining Fatigue and Weakness. Players are only slowed. Replaced rules: 40 degrees Fahrenheit is the freezing-damage cut and food only; 'DC 12 Constitution saves each minute' are the three pulses; 'exhaustion' is the two effects.
item.nusmp.mug_of_the_boss.card:
Consumable (kept, not used up), Rare. A plain ceramic mug carved with odd runes that read "World's Best Boss".
Sneak while you drink to change the word (Boss, General, Lich, Chef, Wizard); the mug is kept. Otherwise, once every 24 hours (a Minecraft day), chug a full cup: the title takes hold for twenty minutes and the creatures that see the mug are moved. Boss: Hero of the Village, and hostile creatures within twelve blocks under sixty health stop hunting anyone for a minute. General: Strength I and Speed I, shared with your pets. Lich: undead within sixteen blocks stop hunting anyone for a minute, Night Vision, Poison Resistance lent. Chef: a full meal and Regeneration. Wizard: Sage and Magic Sense lent, a third of your magicules back.
The flaws: while a title lasts you sing in the water (notes and a banjo), you volunteer for everything (it costs you nothing: the hunger drain of old is gone) and you cannot steer (bad luck while riding a boat or a minecart).
Tabletop became: "advantage on charisma checks" is the awe above; "disadvantage operating a vehicle" is bad luck; "volunteering" is only flavour now; "wisdom save 15" is a health threshold.
item.nusmp.corpse_eater.card: Needs attunement. Frenzy form: reach is 2 blocks longer (10 feet) and every blow adds 3.5 necrotic damage. Right-click: The Eye Opens, creatures in a 12-block cone who can see it must resist (about 40 percent for mobs, 30 for players, 75 or more for bosses) or be paralysed (3 seconds at most for players, 5 for mobs); a creature that resists is immune for 5 minutes (the card's hour). It costs 1 percent of your existence points and recharges in a minute. Sneak-click: Rending Bite, 8 necrotic damage and a festering wound to the foe in front of you, and you heal 3. Feeding Frenzy: whenever a living creature dies within 36 blocks (120 feet) you gain Haste, Speed (and Strength on the third) for 8 seconds and pay one percent of your magicules: the "immediate action" became the faster swings.
item.nusmp.axe_of_the_exile.card: Throw the Axe (use, 2.5 s): the axe flies up to 20 blocks along your line of sight, hits the nearest foe for 6 damage and is back in your hand at once (the card's Returning; the cooldown is its flight). Cursed, Exile: while you hold it (either hand) within 160 blocks of your bed (or the world spawn if you have none), the axe wears you out with Mining Fatigue (the card's exhaustion; your food bar is never touched), and it tells you why once. Far from home the curse turns: you walk 10% faster. The curse ends when you put the axe away. The card's 'cannot speak to loved ones' has no meaning here and is not played.
item.nusmp.ring_of_endless_rage.card:
Requires attunement (the card asks for a barbarian; any attuned bearer may wear it). Carried as a Charm.
The blow that would kill you (after armour and absorption) instead crushes the ruby: you are left on half a heart and rage for 30 seconds. While raging you cannot die (damage can never take you under half a heart), you cannot be healed, and you have Strength II and Speed. When the rage ends you roll three death saves (d20, ten or more holds): 3 saves wake you at half health with Regeneration, 2 at 30%, 1 at 10% weak and slow, none at half a heart, weak and slow. Nothing kills outright. The ring is used up and cannot be used again.
Tabletop became: "drop to zero hit points, crush the ruby" is the lethal blow; "stabilised, cannot die, cannot be healed" is the guarded 30 seconds; the death saves decide the aftermath instead of death.
item.nusmp.fenrirs_collar.card:
Worn at the neck. Requires attunement. Unique.
The card's lycanthropy requirement is dropped (any wearer may attune): the wolf is the collar's own power.
Metamorphose (use): take the cursed hybrid form: +4 attack damage, +20% movement speed, +6 maximum health, +0.3 knockback resistance, night vision, Tensura's godwolf sense and strengthened body lent.
Under the full moon at night, or while a Moon Vigil still holds (until the next full moon), you keep control: the form lasts 5 minutes. At any other time the wolf is not yours: the form slips after 90 seconds and the curse takes its price (Weakness for 30 seconds).
Moon Vigil (sneak and use, once a day): a night at the full moon under the open sky. You heal 6 and Regeneration; until the next full moon (eight days) you hold the wolf.
Shed the Form (third ability): end the form at will, with no price.
Tabletop rules replaced: long rest (a day), the full moon (the moon phase of the world), "loss of control" (the cursed form's price).
item.nusmp.executioners_bane.card:
Drunk and used up. Unique.
Drink it and for three hours of the day (3000 ticks) you survive being beheaded. In the game:
- A blow that would kill you leaves you on one hit point instead (with Resistance V for three seconds), once every ten seconds. A second killing blow inside those ten seconds is the head being destroyed and kills you as it would.
- The head still feels everything (Tensura's pain nullification is lent); but you are slowed and weakened, and you cannot eat or drink while it lasts.
- The head can be reattached: sleep through a night in a bed, or be cured by the Sunheart Medallion's Greater Restoration, Heal, Regenerate or Resurrection. The wound heals and the effect ends.
- If the three hours pass without that, the body gives out: you lose half your health (never the last point), and are slow and weak for a while. (The card says you die; nothing in this game kills outright.)
Tabletop rules replaced: head and body as separate targets, saving throw failures, spell and potion rules (dropped; the survival and its price are what is played).
item.nusmp.perculiar_puking_poison.card:
Drunk and used up. Special.
Make a Constitution save (a d20 plus one for every four points of maximum health above 20, against 15; the card's DC 15). On a fail you are poisoned for one hour of the day (1000 ticks: Weakness all the while, Nausea at each puke) and about every ten minutes of it (167 ticks) you puke up something strange: six times, each a d20:
1 luminous rainbow slime (3 slimeballs, glowing); 2 a broom (a stick and wheat); 3 several large rocks (4 cobblestone); 4 acid (2 damage, corrosion or poison); 5 a live fish (a cod); 6 bubbles (water breathing, slow fall); 7 a book; 8 blood (1d4 damage, never the last point); 9 1d6 carrots; 10 a ship's anchor (2 iron ingots, 3 chains, slowness); 11 live ducklings (three baby chickens that go after two and a half minutes); 12 a well-crafted chair (oak stairs); 13 necrotic mush (rotten flesh); 14 a fist-sized ball of glass; 15 a large cactus (2); 16 a swarm of bugs (spider eyes, nausea); 17 deer antlers (bones); 18 a copy of your own head (your player head); 19 electrical plasma (4 lightning damage to every foe within 3 blocks, you slowed); 20 a full size coffin (a chest and a bone).
item.nusmp.hand_of_vecna.card:
Artifact (God grade), worn in the Hands slot, requires attunement. In the tabletop rules you cut off your left hand and press the Hand to the stump; here the five-second attunement ritual is the cutting, and the first second it works for you it GRAFTS: it cannot be taken off while you live (Curios refuses; an operator frees you with /vecna release <player>; your death frees it and it drops). The game has no alignment: the evil of the Hand is its Whisper.
Strength 20: +7 attack damage, +3 armor and +2 armor toughness while it is worn.
Cold blows: every melee blow adds 3 cold damage (1.5 on a player) and a few seconds of Tensura frost and slowness.
Touch of Death (3% existence points, 60 s cooldown): the creature you touch takes 20 heavy damage and Wither II; a player takes at most 45% of their health and is never left under a heart.
Rimed Grasp (5% mana, 30 s): every foe within six blocks takes 7 cold damage, frost, Slowness III and freezing.
Skeleton to Jelly (needs the Eye too; 4% existence points, 5 min): the touched creature loses 30% of its maximum health (10% on a boss; a player at most 45%, never below a heart), then Slowness III, Weakness III and Glowing.
Coercion: after any Hand act there is a 20% chance of Vecna's Whisper: 8 seconds of Mining Fatigue and a whisper in chat. It takes nothing from you and never forces an act.
The pair of Vecna (Hand and Eye both worn and attuned to one bearer): immune to poison and disease (poison, hunger, magicule poison and infection are cleansed every second, and Poison Resistance, Paralysis Resistance and Danger Sense are lent); cannot be surprised (the first blow from an attacker in each 20 seconds is turned aside); regeneration of one health every two seconds; safe X-ray (no magicule cost); Skeleton to Jelly and the Wish can be used.
The Wish (the pair): Choose the Wish cycles Full Restore, A Day of Resilience, Clear Skies, Summon Rain; Make the Wish grants the chosen one, once in 30 real days for each player.
item.nusmp.eye_of_vecna.card:
Artifact (God grade), worn on the Head, requires attunement. In the tabletop rules you gouge out your eye and press the Eye into the socket; here the five-second attunement ritual is the pressing, and the first second it works for you it GRAFTS: it carries the curse of binding and cannot be taken off while you live (an operator frees you with /vecna release <player>; your death frees it and it drops).
Sight: lends Eye of Truth and Farsight, night vision, and X-ray: every second, mobs and players within 24 blocks that you cannot see glow through the walls (it costs a sliver of magicules unless the pair is worn).
Clairvoyance (4% mana, 60 s): names the five nearest living things within 96 blocks with their coordinates, and makes them glow for ten seconds.
Crown of Madness (3% mana, 45 s): the mob you look at (not a boss) fights its own allies for ten seconds.
Disintegrate (3% existence points, 60 s): a grey beam of 26 heavy damage; it removes no block; a player takes at most 45% of their health and is never left under a heart.
Dominate Monster (6% mana, 2 min): the mob you look at (not a boss, not a player) is your ally for one minute.
Eyebite (3% mana, 30 s): a cone twelve blocks long of Tensura fear, Weakness II and Slowness II for ten seconds (four on a player).
Vecna's Hunger: each use of the Eye has a 5% chance of it: for 20 seconds you are in darkness and slowed and a spectral hand hunts you alone. Kill it. It cannot take your last heart, drops nothing, and never takes control of you or locks you out.
The pair of Vecna (Hand and Eye both worn and attuned to one bearer): immune to poison and disease (poison, hunger, magicule poison and infection are cleansed every second, and Poison Resistance, Paralysis Resistance and Danger Sense are lent); cannot be surprised (the first blow from an attacker in each 20 seconds is turned aside); regeneration of one health every two seconds; safe X-ray (no magicule cost); Skeleton to Jelly and the Wish can be used.
item.nusmp.the_infinity_gauntlet.card:
Artifact (Genesis grade), worn in the Hands slot, requires attunement. Any Infinity Stone you carry anywhere on you (inventory or Curios) is set in the Gauntlet and answers through it; the Gauntlet must be worn. Each carried Stone makes the Stones' acts 12% stronger (range, time, damage), up to +72% with all six, and a worn Gauntlet lends the skills of the Space, Mind, Time and Soul Stones and the pool doubling of the Power Stone even if the Stones are only carried. (The card's rule that the Gauntlet's bearer cannot attune other items is replaced by the usual limit of three attuned relics; the Stones themselves need no attunement slot.)
Greater Wish (all six Stones carried, once a game day): Choose the Wish cycles Treasure (32 diamonds and 32 emeralds), Restoration (every player and pet of yours within 48 blocks healed to full and cleansed), Resistance (Resistance II, Fire Resistance, Water Breathing for 10 minutes), Immunity (cleansed now and every second for a day), Reroll (the blow you took in the last six seconds is healed back).
The Snap (all six Stones carried, once a game day, 10% existence points): every hostile mob within 48 blocks loses half of its current health (a boss a tenth of its maximum), is weakened and slowed, never to zero; no player is touched and no block is changed. The bearer pays with 30 seconds of Weakness II and Mining Fatigue II.
Acts: Space, Mind, Power, Time, Reality, Soul Stone (each needs its Stone carried).
item.nusmp.paradox.card:
Artifact staff (God grade), requires attunement. +3 damage and 2d4 more on every melee blow (the card's 2d10 scaled to a Minecraft blow; half of that on a player) and a critical blow (x1.5) on 19 or 20 of a d20.
Twenty charges, refilled by 2d8+4 at each dawn (a long or short rest). Acts (sneak-use picks the second): Slow (3 charges: foes within 10 blocks, Slowness III and Weakness); Phase Lock (5: the creature you look at is held, for as long as the control caps allow: 5 s on a mob, 3 s on a player, 1 s on a boss); Phase Stasis (3: the same for a person: a player, villager, illager, piglin or witch); Temporal Movement (3: Speed II and Haste II for 15 s); Time Stop (9: every foe within 16 blocks is held, you move at Speed III); Alternate Reality (3: foes within 18 blocks lose their target and stumble for 5 s); Turn the Clock (1: the damaged item in your off hand is turned back to new; not a relic); Missing Time (3: everyone within 18 blocks, you included, saves against DC 15 or is aged (slow and weak) or made young (regenerating and quick) for 20 s).
The Paradox: Time Stop and Missing Time force the staff: you save against DC 17 (d20, only a 17 or more holds); on a failure you are cast out of the timeline back to where you stood about ten seconds ago, tired (Slowness), and the madness table rolls: 0 you are knocked flat; 1-49 short-term (nausea and slowness for 1d10 x 10 s); 50-99 long-term (5 minutes of nausea, weakness and mining fatigue); 100 indefinite (10 minutes, or until milk). The staff's sentience and its habit of vanishing into the timeline are not played.
item.nusmp.sorrows_edge.card: A black crescent axe with a spirit in it that speaks to the one who chose it as a weapon. A heavy axe (10 attack damage) that deals 1d4 necrotic (+2.5 damage) on every hit. A chaotic spirit curses the wielder with a form of the Geas spell: each Minecraft day, the first time you hold it, a percentile die is rolled. At 50 or above you keep your sanity and nothing happens. Below 50 the spirit makes a demand for the day: Blood (kill something within five minutes or take 4 damage and long Weakness and Slowness) or a Fast (eat nothing until dawn; each meal makes you nauseous and weak). The geas is lifted at the next dawn. Tabletop rules replaced: the DM chooses what the spirit demands = one of two demands chosen by the die; percentile roll = the same die; geas = the daily demand.
nusmp.page.book_food.rotten_feast: Leftovers forgotten for a month, served with a smile. A spoiled dish (6 damage) bursts where it lands into a stinking cloud of radius 3.2 that lasts 4 seconds: every enemy inside takes 2.5 damage every half second and is given Mining Fatigue III, Poison II, Weakness and, unless it is a boss, nausea.
nusmp.skill.book_food.description: Food Magic turns the table into a battlefield. The mage conjures giant cutlery that skewers and carves, throws pies and spoiled dishes that slow, sicken and sap enemies, and sets feasts that heal, feed and refill the magicules of allies. Its pages run from fork and knife strikes and a starving rush, through meals and a stomach that eats incoming projectiles, to the banquet table, the wolf of Glutton's Banquet that devours enemy spells, and the once-a-day Midnight Feast. Summon your grimoire, select a page, and press the skill key to cast.
mechanic.nusmp.floor.meshi_hunger.desc: Everything on this floor is a little bit hungry, and it feeds on you: the deeper the floor, the more of your magicules it gnaws (your food bar is never touched), and only a proper meal laid out for it puts it right.
mechanic.nusmp.floor.meshi_hunger.e_cook: Everything on this floor is a little bit hungry, and it feeds on you: the deeper the floor, the more of your magicules it gnaws (your food bar is never touched), and only a proper meal laid out for it puts it right. Hunger bites, but it also bargains: a smell of stew restores a share of health with each wave.
mechanic.nusmp.floor.meshi_hunger.t_spri: Everything on this floor is a little bit hungry, and it feeds on you: the deeper the floor, the more of your magicules it gnaws (your food bar is never touched), and only a proper meal laid out for it puts it right. Running in its area sets it off.
mechanic.nusmp.floor.meshi_hunger.c_item: Everything on this floor is a little bit hungry, and it feeds on you: the deeper the floor, the more of your magicules it gnaws (your food bar is never touched), and only a proper meal laid out for it puts it right. Lay an offering on its altar to quiet it.
mechanic.nusmp.floor.meshi_hunger.e_shak: Everything on this floor is a little bit hungry, and it feeds on you: the deeper the floor, the more of your magicules it gnaws (your food bar is never touched), and only a proper meal laid out for it puts it right. A starving hand shakes: every wave also breaks the grip on every item for a few seconds.
mechanic.nusmp.floor.meshi_hunger.t_hp_b: Everything on this floor is a little bit hungry, and it feeds on you: the deeper the floor, the more of your magicules it gnaws (your food bar is never touched), and only a proper meal laid out for it puts it right. It smells a wounded delver and strikes when someone drops under half health.
